URL: https://www.iranintl.com/en/202611201108
Iran International, 20 November 2026

Speaking at the University of Tehran, Mohebbi referred to an August 26 warning by senior armed forces spokesman Abolfazl Shekarchi, who threatened to designate Iran International, BBC Persian, Radio Farda and their employees as military targets.

“We have announced that some media outlets are our targets, such as Iran International,” Mohebbi said, referring to the earlier announcement by Iran's military leadership.

“They are our targets because they are acting with hostility. They are not impartial media outlets,” he added.

Shekarchi had accused the broadcasters of links to US and Israeli intelligence services without presenting evidence.

The renewed threat comes a week after two Iranian men were convicted in London of assisting a foreign intelligence service in a case involving surveillance of Iran International journalists and preparations for violence in Britain.

Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, were convicted at Woolwich Crown Court on November 12. The court heard that the men had monitored journalists Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, as well as British lawyer Jonathan Turner, on behalf of Iranian intelligence.

Sepahvand was also convicted of preparing to commit serious violence against a person in Britain. Prosecutors said he had been promised up to £150,000, approximately $200,000, to carry out an attack.

Both men are due to be sentenced on December 17. A third defendant was acquitted.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned Monday that Britain would respond to Iranian-sponsored attacks on journalists, Jewish communities and military airbases.

“We cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon, nor to massacre their own people and threaten the region unchecked. Nor will we allow them to sponsor attacks on journalists, our Jewish communities here in Britain and airbases without response. Nor will we allow them to sponsor attacks on journalists, our Jewish communities here in Britain and airbases without response,” Burnham said at the Lord Mayor's Banquet in London.

Months of threats against Iran International

Mohebbi's remarks follow a series of threats against Iran International, its journalists and broadcasting infrastructure during the war.

In March, the government-aligned Tabnak website called for attacks on the broadcaster and people associated with it, including offices and homes of some employees and analysts in Israel.

Later that month, Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters threatened facilities supporting Iran International's broadcasts, accusing the network of psychological warfare.

The Committee to Protect Journalists reported that Iranian authorities had warned Turkmenistan and Monaco over satellite services carrying the broadcaster's programming. Interference with its satellite signals was also reported.

In April, Iran International said Iranian state television had repeatedly aired calls for missile strikes against the broadcaster.

The network also reported financial and judicial measures affecting more than 100 people, including 63 of its journalists, as well as pressure on employees' families.

Three people were charged with arson with intent to endanger life following an April 15 incident in which an incendiary device was thrown towards a building near Iran International's London studios, landing in a car park.

Their trial was scheduled to begin on January 25, 2027, at London's Central Criminal Court. The Committee to Protect Journalists confirmed on November 13 that proceedings in the case remained ongoing.

"])•••$RC("B:5","S:5")More StoriesBessent's relocation linked to Iran chemical threat – NYTNov 19, 2026, 01:42 GMT+0Listen to this article100%US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks during the National Committee on US-China Relations 60th Anniversary Gala Dinner in New York City, US, November 10, 2026. REUTERSUS Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's relocation to a military base was linked to Israeli intelligence about an alleged Iranian plot to use chemical agents against senior American officials, The New York Times reported Wednesday, citing a person briefed on the intelligence.

Bessent relocated from his Washington-area home to a military base earlier this month following threats attributed to Iran. In a Friday interview with CNBC, he said he had followed Secret Service instructions and would not be intimidated by the threats.

The Treasury secretary has spearheaded Washington's economic pressure campaign against Iran, including Operation Economic Outcast, launched in August to tighten sanctions and financial restrictions and pressure Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The reported threat comes amid broader US intelligence concerns about possible Iranian attacks against senior American officials.

CNN reported Monday, citing seven US officials, that intelligence indicated Iran was developing plans to potentially target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a radioactive dirty bomb or chemical weapon.

US officials differed over whether Iran had the capability or intention to carry out such an attack.

President Donald Trump said Tuesday that Washington was examining the intelligence and warned Iran of severe consequences if it carried out an attack.

“Well, if there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before,” Trump told reporters in Manila when asked whether an attack was imminent.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that he did not believe Washington faced an imminent threat.

“I don't think there is any imminent threat,” Rubio told reporters, adding that US authorities remained alert to potential dangers.

Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected the allegations as baseless. The White House said it was monitoring potential threats but had identified no credible threat to the US homeland at that time.

Israeli officials have also warned that Iran could equip drones with chemical or biological weapons to attack Israel or neighboring countries, according to the Times.

US intelligence officials have identified indications of Iranian efforts to strengthen chemical and biological weapons capabilities, the newspaper reported. However, the Times said US intelligence officials largely assessed that Iran was developing those capabilities as a deterrent against major US or Israeli attacks, rather than for preemptive use.

US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told a congressional hearing Wednesday that threats from Iran against Americans at home and abroad had increased substantially, although he declined to discuss specific intelligence about the reported Washington attack plot.

Listen to this article100%Lebanon’s Hezbollah, acting under the IRGC Quds Force’s direction, recruited six Thai clerics who had studied in Qom for a plot to attack the Israeli embassy in Bangkok, a Western intelligence source and a source close to the Quds Force told Iran International.

The sources identified the six men as recruits of Unit 910, the overseas operations unit of the Iran-backed Lebanese group. They said the plot was thwarted.

One member of the network said a Lebanese man he knew as Abu Hassan was his direct handler and supplied him with information for the planned attack.

The two sources identified Abu Hassan as Majed Abdullah, also known as Fadi Kassab, and said he began recruiting students at Al-Mustafa International University in Qom around 2020 with help from the Quds Force.

Kassab’s earlier mission in Bangkok

Kassab’s involvement in Thailand dated back to at least 2012, the sources said. That year, he entered the country under an assumed name to plan and oversee attacks on Israeli interests in Bangkok. The sources identified Hussein Atris, a Swedish-Lebanese national arrested at Bangkok airport that year, as one of his operatives.

100%Atris led Thai police to a warehouse outside the capital where bomb-making materials had been stored. A Thai court convicted him the following year of illegally possessing the materials.

The two sources said Kassab prepared recruits for Unit 910 and had also been linked to operations in Cyprus, Bulgaria, the United States and Canada. They described a division of responsibilities in Iran. A Lebanese national named Mohammad Hassan oversaw Hezbollah’s operations in the country and trained recruits, while Kassab planned attacks on Israeli interests.

100%From Qom’s seminaries to Bangkok

At the center of the Thai network, the sources said, was Mubarak Hosseini, a cleric who had spent more than three decades in Iran and later became head of Al-Mustafa’s alumni association.

100%His family’s ties to Iran went back to 1985, when his cousin Salman Hosseini, a Shia cleric, came to the country and was recruited by the Hojjatieh Association, the sources said. Salman subsequently made regular trips to Thailand to recruit others, including Mubarak.

In a 2023 interview with the Iranian publication Ofogh-e Howzeh, Mubarak said he arrived in Iran in 1991 and studied first at Qom’s seminary, then at the International Centre for Islamic Studies. He later pursued a doctorate in political science at Al-Mustafa, which was founded in 2008 on the orders of then-Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.
